answer: Treat identity as a maturity ladder, not a flag: a new key starts at its nadir, a vertex with zero weight, and earns standing only by finishing randomized micro-tasks spread over several epochs, each keyed to a fresh beacon so no work can be stockpiled or bought ahead. One honest sparrow matures in real time; a farm must push every clone through the same unpredictable months, paying compute and coordination per head, while reused task traces collapse the whole flock into one slashed cluster.
